corrected_row: | DOC-A.1-72 | **FILE-CONTROL entry, ASSIGN clause — consistency rules for external file connectors**, §12.4.5 GR1, required + documented | §12.4.5.3 GR1 b) requires the file control entries that reference one external file connector to have *"A consistent specification for data-name-1, device-name-1, and literal-1 in the ASSIGN clause"* and leaves the rules to the implementor. **COBOL.NET's rule: the entries must name the same file target and the same data-name-1, and nothing more.** (1) **The TO phrase is compared by the operand that names the file** (item 71), not by every word written: a leading device class is dropped, a literal is compared by its value and a device-name by its spelling. So `ASSIGN TO DISK "xa.dat"`, `ASSIGN TO PRINTER "xa.dat"` and `ASSIGN TO "xa.dat"` are consistent, and a device-name and a literal with the same spelling are the same name, so `ASSIGN TO XADAT` and `ASSIGN TO "xadat"` are consistent. Item 71's host-path mapping is NOT applied before the comparison: `ASSIGN TO XADAT` and `ASSIGN TO "xadat.txt"` are NOT consistent, although both open the host file `xadat.txt`. The comparison ignores case, so `"Data.txt"` and `"data.txt"` are consistent, even though on a case-sensitive host they name different physical files; the file opened is the one named in the program that executes the OPEN. An entry with a TO phrase and one without are not consistent. (2) **The USING data-name-1 is compared by spelling, qualifiers included, ignoring case.** `IN` and `OF` are the same, so `FNAME IN G` and `FNAME OF G` are consistent; `FNAME` and `FNAME OF G` are not, and neither are an entry with a USING phrase and one without. The check runs only when checking for EC-EXTERNAL-FILE-MISMATCH is enabled. It happens when a second program that describes the external file is activated: the two ASSIGN fields are part of the `SelectFingerprint` each program registers with `ExternalStore.Describe` (built in `OoEmitter.EmitExternalDescribes`), and a difference raises **EC-EXTERNAL-FILE-MISMATCH** (§14.8.4.4), which is fatal. **⛔ The two programs still hold SEPARATE STORAGE for an identically-spelled data-name-1, and that is deliberate.** §12.4.5.3 GR3 b) associates the connector with the file named *"in the runtime element that executes the OPEN, SORT, or MERGE statement"*, which only makes sense if the entries MAY name different data items. GR1 i) shows how the standard words it when it wants the opposite (FILE STATUS: *"where data-name-4 shall reference the same corresponding external data item"*), and §13.4.5.4 GR2 c) 2. does the same for LINAGE; GR1 b) says neither. Implemented at `FileConnector.Associate`, called with the executing program's own rendered specification (kb/Work PB673). | — |

corrected_row: | DOC-A.1-74 | **Figurative constant values — representation of ZERO, SPACE and QUOTE**, §8.3.3.6 (§8.3.3.6.4 GR1), required + documented | Each has ONE representation, the same code unit in both coded character sets (both are UTF-16, one code unit per character position — item 33): **SPACE is U+0020, ZERO is U+0030 (the character '0'), QUOTE is U+0022 (the character '"')**. In an alphanumeric item that is the one-byte DISPLAY image 0x20 / 0x30 / 0x22 (item 209); in a national item it is the two-byte code unit 0x0020 / 0x0030 / 0x0022 (two bytes per national position, as item 209's row states). So, with no PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE, `MOVE SPACE` to a `PIC X` item gives `FUNCTION ORD` 33, ZERO 49, QUOTE 35, and the national item gives the same values (ORD reports the position in the program collating sequence, so under `PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE IS` an EBCDIC alphabet it reports 65 for SPACE although the stored character is still U+0020); `SPACE = X"20"`, `QUOTE = X"22"`, `ZERO = X"30"` and `QUOTE = NX"0022"` are all true. Neither a PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE, an ALPHABET clause nor a CODE-SET clause changes these values in storage; those clauses affect comparison order and the file's external code set only. The single source for the fill characters is `FigurativeConstants.FillChar`. (A BOOLEAN receiver is outside this item: ZERO fills it with the boolean character '0', and so does SPACE, determination D-B2 in §3.) | — |

corrected_record.notes: Row states the representation of ZERO/SPACE/QUOTE (§8.3.3.6.4 1), cite.py OK). Probe /tmp/adj/doc/doc-w1-s3/probe/p74.cob at --std 2014 and 2023: ORD of SPACE/ZERO/QUOTE in PIC X = 33/49/35, in PIC N = 33/49/35; SPACE=X"20", QUOTE=X"22", ZERO=X"30", national QUOTE = NX"0022" all true. At --std 85 the alphanumeric half holds and national data is gated (COBOLNET0900). FigurativeConstants.FillChar: 'Z'->'0', 'S'->' ', 'Q'->'"'. No spec-derived test pins the code values, so test-ref is empty. Row closes the documentation gap owned by kb/Work/PB1397 (item 74).

reason: Values confirmed (refute-probe/r74.cob: ORD 33/49/35 in X and N, SPACE=X"20", ZERO=X"30", QUOTE=X"22", QUOTE=NX"0022"; §8.3.3.6.4 1) cite.py OK). CORRECTION: the ORD example is true only in the native collating sequence - refute-probe/r74c.cob with PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE IS EBCDIC: ORD(SPACE)=65 while the record written holds 20 30 22; r74d.cob CODE-SET EBCDIC writes 40 F0 7F. corrected_row: | DOC-A.1-95 | **Hexadecimal alphanumeric literals — result when no corresponding character exists**, §8.3.3.2 GR4 (printed as §8.3.3.2.4 GR5 in this text), required + documented | **The case does not arise: every hex-character-sequence has a corresponding character.** A hexadecimal alphanumeric literal takes TWO hexadecimal digits per character (§8.3.3.2.3 SR6; any other count is refused, COBOLNET1635), and the group `hh` is the character whose code is U+00hh, which is also its one-byte DISPLAY image (item 209). All 256 values 00 through FF are characters of the alphanumeric set, so each group is stored as that character, including the control codes 00–1F, 7F and 80–9F, with no diagnostic and no exception condition. Example: `X"80FF0041"` is four characters whose `FUNCTION ORD` values are 129, 256, 1 and 66. What a device shows for a control character on DISPLAY is the device's business, not the literal's. Implemented in `CobolLiteral.DecodeHex`. | — |

Probe /tmp/adj/doc/doc-w1-s3/probe/p95.cob at 2014/2023: X"80FF0041" ORD 129 256 1 66, LENGTH 4; p95b.cob DISPLAY X"80FF41" prints U+0080 U+00FF 'A' (UTF-8 C2 80 C3 BF 41). corrected_row: | DOC-A.1-97 | **Hexadecimal national literals — result when no corresponding character exists**, §8.3.3.5 GR4 (printed as §8.3.3.5.4 GR5 in this text), required + documented | A hexadecimal national literal takes FOUR hexadecimal digits per character (§8.3.3.5.3 SR5; any other count is refused, COBOLNET1635), and each group is stored **verbatim as that UTF-16 code unit**, the national character representation (item 33). A group that is not a character on its own, such as a surrogate half D800–DFFF or a noncharacter such as FFFE or FFFF, is stored unchanged, as one character position, with no diagnostic and no exception condition. It then behaves as any other national character: `FUNCTION LENGTH(NX"D800")` is 1, `FUNCTION ORD` gives the code plus 1 (55297 for D800, 65536 for FFFF), and comparison uses the code unit's value. Two groups that form a valid surrogate pair stay two character positions. On DISPLAY to a UTF-8 device, an unpaired surrogate is written as U+FFFD. Implemented in `CobolLiteral.DecodeHexGroups`. | — |

corrected_row: | DOC-A.1-79 | **FLAG-02 directive — the warning mechanism**, §7.3.14 GR1 (§7.3.14.4 GR1), required + documented | **A compile-time warning, COBOLNET1620, for each flagged construct. The warning does not change the compiled program.** `>>FLAG-02` names ALL, or one or more of its five options (EC-PROGRAM-EXCEPTIONS, I-O-STATUS-07, MOVE-TO-SAME-NAME, RANGE-EXCEPTION-FOR-INDEX, TERMINATE-WITH-VARYING) in any order, followed by ON or OFF. If ON and OFF are both omitted, ON applies. An option is on from the line after the directive until a later FLAG-02 turns it off, or turns ALL off, or the compilation group ends. Every option is off by default. While an option is on, each construct §7.3.14.4 GR4 describes for it is reported as `warning COBOLNET1620: <the construct> (<the 2002-to-2014 change>) — flagged by >>FLAG-02 <option>` at the construct's line and column. For example, with I-O-STATUS-07 on, each `CLOSE ... WITH NO REWIND` or `UNIT` is reported. An option word that is not one of the five, or ALL combined with named options, is refused with COBOLNET1622. The directive is a COBOL-2014 element: at `--std 2002` and below it is refused with COBOLNET0900, and at `--std 2023` it still works but draws the obsolete-element warning COBOLNET0903 (§7.3.14.1 NOTE). Known defects in the open notes, not part of this determination: `>>FLAG-02 ON`, `>>FLAG-02 OFF` and a bare `>>FLAG-02` (the printed format leaves ALL un-underlined, so ALL is the default) are currently refused with COBOLNET1622, so write ALL explicitly, and a repeated option word is silently accepted instead of refused (kb/Work PB1374); the EC-PROGRAM-EXCEPTIONS warnings have no source location and are reported once per program (kb/Work PB1376), and some GR4 construct populations are narrower than the rule (kb/Work PB1375). Implemented by `FlagDirectiveLine.TryParse`, `FlagState` and `FlagConformancePass`; the diagnostic is `DiagnosticCatalog.Flag02Warning`. | `unit:FlagDirectiveTests.Compile_Flag02IoStatus07On_EmitsCobolnet1620_OnEachPhraseSpelling`; `unit:FlagDirectiveTests.Parse_Flag02_OnIsImplicit_WhenOnOffOmitted`; `unit:FlagDirectiveTests.Fold_DefaultsOff_AndIsStickyForwardStrictlyAfterTheDirective` |

corrected_row: | DOC-A.1-80 | **FLAG-14 directive — the warning mechanism**, §7.3.15 GR1 (§7.3.15.4 GR1), required + documented | **A compile-time warning, COBOLNET1621, for each flagged construct. The warning does not change the compiled program.** `>>FLAG-14` names ALL, or one or more of its twelve options (COMPILE-TIME-ARITHMETIC-EXPRESSIONS, EVALUATE, I-O-DECLARATIVE, I-O-STATUS-04, I-O-STATUS-07, NUM-ED-ZERO-FIGCONST, READ-PREVIOUS, REF-MOD-ZERO-LENGTH, VALUE-EDITING, VALUE-FIG-CON-LENGTH, VALUE-ZERO, WRITE-END-OF-PAGE) in any order, followed by ON or OFF. An option is on from the line after the directive until a later FLAG-14 turns it off, or turns ALL off, or the compilation group ends. Every option is off by default. While an option is on, each construct §7.3.15.4 GR4 describes for it is reported as `warning COBOLNET1621: <the construct> (<the 2014-to-2023 change>) — flagged by >>FLAG-14 <option>` at the construct's line and column. For example, `>>FLAG-14 READ-PREVIOUS I-O-STATUS-04 ON` reports each READ PREVIOUS statement and each reference that tests a FILE STATUS item for '04', and `>>FLAG-14 VALUE-ZERO ON` reports a numeric-edited item whose VALUE is ZERO. An option word that is not one of the twelve, or ALL combined with named options, is refused with COBOLNET1622. The directive is COBOL-2023 only: at `--std 2014` and below it is refused with COBOLNET0900. Known defects in the open notes, not part of this determination: an omitted ON/OFF is currently refused with COBOLNET1622 instead of meaning ON, and an omitted option list (`>>FLAG-14 ON`, `>>FLAG-14 OFF`, where ALL is the default) is refused the same way, so write ON and ALL explicitly; a repeated option word is silently accepted instead of refused (kb/Work PB1374); and some GR4 construct populations are narrower than the rule, for example the arithmetic expression of a constant entry is not examined under COMPILE-TIME-ARITHMETIC-EXPRESSIONS (kb/Work PB1375). corrected_row: | DOC-A.1-100 | **Implementor-defined level-2 exception conditions, EC-level-2-IMP — specification and meaning of each specified level-2 IMP exception condition**, §14.6.13.1.6 Table 13 (§14.6.13.1.1, the '-IMP' suffix type), optional + documented if provided | **Provided: 20 of Table 13's 22 EC-level-2-IMP names are valid exception-names, and each is FATAL.** Table 13's 22 names are EC-ARGUMENT-IMP, EC-BOUND-IMP, EC-CONTINUE-IMP, EC-DATA-IMP, EC-EXTERNAL-IMP, EC-FLOW-IMP, EC-FUNCTION-IMP, EC-I-O-IMP, EC-LOCALE-IMP, EC-MCS-IMP, EC-OO-IMP, EC-ORDER-IMP, EC-OVERFLOW-IMP, EC-PROGRAM-IMP, EC-RAISING-IMP, EC-RANGE-IMP, EC-REPORT-IMP, EC-SCREEN-IMP, EC-SIZE-IMP, EC-SORT-MERGE-IMP, EC-STORAGE-IMP and EC-VALIDATE-IMP. EC-CONTINUE-IMP, EC-EXTERNAL-IMP and EC-MCS-IMP are COBOL-2023 names; below 2023 they are refused with COBOLNET0878. EC-SCREEN-IMP and EC-VALIDATE-IMP belong to the screen and VALIDATE modules, which this implementation does not provide (Annex A.4.2, A.4.14). They are refused wherever they are written, with COBOLNET1707 and COBOLNET1710. The other 20 can be used in `>>TURN`, `RAISE EXCEPTION` and wherever an exception-name is allowed. Table 13 leaves their fatality to the implementor (Imp), and this implementation treats every one as fatal. An unhandled one ends the run unit abnormally, and so does a `RAISE EXCEPTION` of one with checking not enabled. **Meaning: the implementation itself sets only EC-PROGRAM-IMP**, and only when a contained program is activated while the program that contains it has no instance (an internal consistency failure of the program table, reported as 'internal: contained program ... activated while its container is not instantiated'). The implementation never sets any of the others, so a program sees them only when it raises them itself. EC-I-O-IMP is Table 13's 'I-O status 9x' condition, but the only 9x status COBOL.NET defines, '90', carries EC-I-O-LINAGE instead (item 110). EC-RAISING-IMP is never set at run time either. The names and fatality are `ExceptionCatalog` (EcFatality.Imp); the one raise site is `ProgramTable.ParentInstance`, through the default exception-name of `CobolCallException`. | — |
